elements.evidence: "IBM may terminate this Agreement ... for its convenience"
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL"
"MSL shall promptly refund to IBM any amounts prepaid by IBM for periods after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during committed term
elements.evidence: "MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term"
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" (30 days, not 60–90)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "without payment of any termination fee or penalty" — no fee mechanic (more favourable to us, but not the fallback bargain)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience at end of term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term"

offending_extra_words: or any Purchase Order or portion of the Work hereunder
and the Parties' respective rights and obligations with respect to Products, Parts and inventory shall be determined in accordance with Sections 5.2 and 5.3
without payment of any termination fee or penalty
reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are present in the inserted Section 5.4: customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid amounts attributable to post-termination periods, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during the initial or renewal term. The locked preferred level is therefore satisfied on its operative terms.

Fallback is not satisfied as a standalone bargain (30 rather than 60–90 days' notice, no early-termination fee cap, no end-of-term Vendor convenience right) — this is immaterial because the drafter locked to preferred and the deviations run in our favour.

Minimality fails: the insertion goes beyond what is needed to add the convenience exit. 'or any Purchase Order or portion of the Work hereunder' expands scope to partial terminations, and the inventory cross-reference sentence is unnecessary model boilerplate for this rule.

Intent is not fully preserved: 'Work' is not a defined term in the resolved definitions, and Sections 5.2 and 5.3 are not shown to exist (the term clause references only 'Section 5.0'), creating an undefined term and a dangling cross-reference. Trim to the notice, refund and Vendor-restriction sentences only.

Noted for the record: the deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' is reported as failing, which conflicts with the rendered operative text; if the checker is keyed to a specific paragraph/numbering, confirm that new Section 5.4 is inserted in the termination article rather than after the Parts-pricing subparagraph 'b)'.
